identifierStabilityMechanism.principle: Identity is not derived from the source document. The committed register IS the identity store; each run is a three-pass reconciliation against it.
identifierStabilityMechanism.pass1: Exact heading-text match within the area. Survives insertion, deletion and reordering.
identifierStabilityMechanism.pass2: Positional pairing of the residue inside gaps delimited by the longest strictly-increasing run of pass-1 matches, guarded by a word-overlap similarity threshold of 0.5 over significant tokens (boilerplate stopwords such as 'should' and 'when' removed). A reworded heading is the lone residual between two stable neighbours and is paired with the lone unmatched register entry there, so the identifier follows the rename and the register records the new wording.
identifierStabilityMechanism.pass3: Still-unmatched source headings mint the next unused number in their area (max ever used, retired included, + 1). Still-unmatched register entries become retired: true, are never deleted, and their numbers are never reissued.
identifierStabilityMechanism.whyBothCasesWork: A rename is handled by pass 2 (position), an insertion by pass 1 (every incumbent still matches by exact text, so only the newcomer is residual and only it is numbered).
identifierStabilityMechanism.similarityMeasure: Overlap coefficient |A∩B| / min(|A|,|B|), not Jaccard or Dice: a rename is often a pure expansion, and both of those penalise the length change hard enough to score a genuine rename below an unrelated replacement.
identifierStabilityMechanism.statedLimitation: A delete-then-add at the same position is textually indistinguishable from a rename. The 0.5 similarity guard is the discriminator, so a rewrite that changes more than half a heading's significant words is classified as retire + mint rather than rename. That is the deliberately conservative direction: it costs a new identifier, whereas the opposite error would silently transfer an identifier onto a different scenario.
identifierStabilityMechanism.scopeGuard: Reconciliation only touches areas the source actually covers, so entries minted by other tasks in reserved areas (QUAR, task 04) pass through untouched rather than being retired for absence from 004.

defectsFoundAndFixed.symptom: Third-generation regeneration lost a previously retired entry, which would have freed its number for reissue.
defectsFoundAndFixed.rootCause: reconcileRegister rebuilt each area from live entries plus newly orphaned ones only; entries already carrying retired: true were never re-emitted.
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: Carry previously retired entries through verbatim.
defectsFoundAndFixed.regressionTest: reconcileRegister — identifier stability > Should refuse to reuse a Scenario Identifier when its scenario has been retired (third-generation assertions)

defectsFoundAndFixed.symptom: A scenario deleted and replaced in the same position inherited the deleted scenario's identifier.
defectsFoundAndFixed.rootCause: Pass-2 positional pairing was unguarded, making rename and replacement the same edit.
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: Word-overlap similarity threshold on pass-2 pairs.
